title: The Cracked Showroom
crime: Last night someone dragged a crate across the showroom's new glass floor and cracked it. Every crate owner gave the clerk their crate's pressure, and one of them lied.
deed: you dragged your crate across the glass floor last night and cracked it, then gave the clerk a false pressure.
oath: My crate presses on the floor at {value} {unit}. Write it down.
measure: The lab weighs each crate and measures the area of its base.
hint: *Pressure is the force spread over the area: divide the weight by the base area.
arrive: Watt Works, and the showroom's glass floor has a crack right across it. The Baron erased the law of pressure.
Three crate owners. Each one told the clerk how hard their crate presses on the floor.
Numbers can lie when people say them. Question them, then check the crates.
inspect: A long scrape and a crack in the glass. Something heavy, on a small base.
Weigh the crates and measure their bases. The pressure tells on whoever lied.
confession: Fine! My crate scraped the glass. The Baron said nobody could check a pressure without the law.
